acceptanceCriteria: A1: docs/reference/collaboration-invariant-coverage.md(+zh-CN/ja) states, for all ten invariants, whether automated coverage exists today, citing the exact test file and function name for each Yes/Partial row, verified by direct reading of the current test source.
A2: gaps are stated precisely (which case is not covered), not just 'no test exists', and each gap names a concrete reuse-based follow-on approach citing an existing pattern to extend.
A3: no claim in this document overstates coverage; a Partial row explains exactly what is and is not covered.
A4: docs/reference/README.md(+zh-CN/ja) gain exactly one new index entry each.
A5: WI-681 registers itself in the reference-parity ledger with the pre-archive status, added before this Work Item's own verification-evidence commit.
A6: bash tests/docs/documentation_acceptance.sh passes for all new and modified files.
goal: A maintainer or reviewer can see, for each invariant, whether an automated regression test already protects it and exactly which one, instead of having to search or re-derive this themselves, and can see a concrete, reuse-based plan for the remaining gaps.
intent: Map each of the ten collaboration-language semantic invariants (from WI-679) to existing automated test coverage in this repository, citing exact test file/function names verified by direct source reading, and name remaining gaps precisely, per explicit repository-owner delegation to continue the AI Cockpit collaboration-language initiative. This is a reuse-first survey, not new test code: per the initiative's own scoping, writing the identified missing tests is deferred to bounded follow-on Work Items named in the delivered document.
outOfScope: writing the four identified missing tests themselves (follow-on Work Items)
any change to CLI/MCP behavior; Contract/Outcome schema; lifecycle state machine
any change to existing test files
